keyword: did the astronauts make it back

verifications.claim: The four Artemis II astronauts safely returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II's astronauts returned from the moon with a dramatic splashdown in the Pacific on Friday... April 10, 2026.'; R2: 'Updated April 10, 2026... The voyage concludes Friday, April 10'; R3: 'Artemis II astronauts are back on Earth... splashed down at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R4: 'successfully splashed down... at 8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm safe splashdown return on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'nearly 10-day flight'; R2: 'historic 10-day journey... 10-day flight... 10 days in space'; R3: 'record-breaking 10-day mission... officially lasted 9 days, 1 hour, 31 minutes'; R4: '10-day journey around the moon... 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly describe it as a 10-day mission, despite precise duration slightly under 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission went around the moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'historic trip around the moon... lunar flyby'; R2: 'circling the moon'; R3: 'journey around the moon'; R4: 'journey around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All references explicitly state the mission involved a trip or flyby around the moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew included NASA's Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canada's Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch of NASA, and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency'; R3 & R4: identical listings
verifications.reasoning: All references list exactly these four astronauts with correct affiliations.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashdown in the Pacific... off the San Diego coast'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3 & R4: 'off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm exact location of splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down at 8:07 p.m. ET.

verifications.reasoning: References directly state the splashdown time as 8:07 p.m. ET.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew reported they were in good shape following their journey.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II journey broke the record for the farthest distance any human has ever traveled from Earth.

verifications.reasoning: References explicitly state it broke the distance record.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft safely completed a high-speed, high-heat reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'hit the atmosphere traveling Mach 33... engulfed in red-hot plasma during peak heating... emerged from its communication blackout'; R3: 'peak heating... Temperatures can be up to 5,000 degrees... perfect descent'; R4: 'Orion came blaring back into Earth’s atmosphere... successfully splashed down'
verifications.reasoning: All describe successful high-speed (Mach 33+, 24,000+ mph), high-heat reentry with safe outcome.
